title: Alchemical Distillation Engine
description: A steampunk-inspired chemistry lab where a translucent teacup serves as a reaction vessel and interlocking gears drive a distillation pump. The user must combine reagents in the correct order, adjust gear speed to control temperature, and manage conservation of mass across distillation cycles, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an Alchemical Distillation Engine. Load DiffuseTransmissionTeacup.glb centered at (0,0,0) as the main reaction vessel and gears.glb positioned to its right at (3,0,0) as the temperature-control mechanism. Use OrbitControls with the camera at (0,3,8) looking at origin. Add ambient light (0.4) and a warm point light above the teacup. The teacup must use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission=0.6 and its liquid color changes based on reagent state. Create an HTML overlay panel on the left with 5 reagent buttons (Sulfur-yellow, Mercury-silver, Salt-white, Aqua Regia-green, Philosopher's Stone-purple). Each reagent click adds it to the vessel, changing the liquid color via additive RGB mixing and incrementing a displayed mass counter. The gears must rotate continuously; add a slider (1-10) controlling gear rotation speed which maps to a temperature gauge (100-1000K) displayed as a colored bar. Implement conservation of mass: total mass across vessel and distillate output (shown as a second smaller sphere at (-3,1,0)) must remain constant. When temperature exceeds a reagent's boiling point, that component transfers from vessel to distillate, reducing vessel mass and increasing distillate mass accordingly. Boiling points: Sulfur=718K, Mercury=630K, Salt=1074K, Aqua Regia=400K, Philosopher's Stone=900K. The user must add reagents in a specific sequence (Aqua Regia, Mercury, Sulfur, Salt, Philosopher's Stone), adjust temperature to selectively distill components, and collect exactly 3 purified outputs to complete the task. Implement undo/redo buttons that revert or replay each discrete action (reagent add, temperature change, distillation event) using a state history stack. Show a step counter out of 14 maximum steps. Display a success message with particle effects when the user correctly isolates 3 distilled components while conserving total mass within 2% tolerance.
